fullPassage:
Resilience: Recovering from Difficult Times

Teenage life on social media might seem fun and easy, but being a real teenager presents its own set of challenges, both big and small. So why can some people handle tough times and become stronger while others remain unchanged and helpless? The answer lies in resilience — the ability to adapt to challenging experiences, such as unexpected events or personal difficulties.

The good news is that humans can recover from pressure and hardship and you can develop this skill. However, having resilience does not mean you will never feel stressed or anxious; it is perfectly normal to feel down every now and then. Resilience will not prevent problems, but it will help you face and overcome them.

Think of it like building your body's immune system. Just as you need to be exposed to germs to build immunity, you must experience difficulties to build resilience. In simple terms, resilience is not about being emotionless: Resilience means you experience. You feel. You fail. You hurt. You fall. But you keep going. It is like working out to build your muscles; it takes time and effort to enhance your resilience.

questions.passage: Teenage life on social media might seem fun and easy, but ①<u>being</u> a real teenager presents its own set of challenges, both big and small. So why can some people handle tough times and become ②<u>more strong</u> while others remain ③<u>unchanged</u> and helpless? The answer lies in resilience — the ability to ④<u>adapt</u> to challenging experiences, such as unexpected events or personal difficulties.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: strong은 1음절 형용사이므로 비교급은 more strong이 아닌 stronger가 되어야 한다.
det.analysis:
❌ ② more strong → stronger: 1음절 형용사 비교급은 -er
✅ ① being: 동명사 주어 (Being a real teenager)
✅ ③ unchanged: remain + 형용사 보어
✅ ④ adapt: the ability to + 동사원형
det.tip: 1음절 형용사 비교급: strong → stronger (more strong ✗). remain + 형용사 (2형식 보어)

questions.passage: The good news is that humans can recover from pressure and hardship and you can develop this skill. However, ①<u>having</u> resilience does not mean you will never feel ②<u>stressed</u> or anxious; it is perfectly normal to feel ③<u>down</u> every now and then. Resilience will not prevent problems, but it will help you ④<u>facing</u> and overcome them.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: help + 목적어 + 동사원형: help you face and overcome이므로 facing이 아닌 face가 되어야 한다.
det.analysis:
❌ ④ facing → face: help + O + V원형 (face and overcome 병렬)
✅ ① having: 동명사 주어
✅ ② stressed: feel + 형용사(과거분사)
✅ ③ down: feel + 형용사(부사 아닌 형용사 down)
det.tip: help + O + (to) V원형. face와 overcome이 and로 병렬 연결

questions.passage: Think of it like building your body's immune system. Just as you need to be ①<u>exposed</u> to germs to build immunity, you must experience difficulties to build resilience. det.korean: ① be exposed to(수동태) ✅ ② about being(전치사+동명사) ✅ ③ keep going(keep+V-ing) ✅ ④ it takes(가주어 구문) ✅ — 모두 어법상 올바르다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① exposed: need to be exposed (수동태)
✅ ② being: about + 동명사
✅ ③ going: keep + V-ing
✅ ④ takes: It takes ~ to V (가주어 구문)
→ 모두 올바르므로 ③ 전부
det.tip: be exposed to(~에 노출되다), keep V-ing(계속 ~하다), It takes ~ to V(~하는 데 ~이 걸리다)
